text:
Faculty Review (SHA1 - ACT201, MMR5 - BUS112, RGC - LAW200, MGT351 - TNN)
*EXCUSE ME FOR THE BANGLISH THOUGH*
RGC - LAW200
I know that LAW department er kono kharap faculty nai ; at least for this course. But trust me when I say, amongst all the great faculties from the LAW Dept, RGC deserves to be in a spot even higher. Why, you might ask? It's because, even though LAW200 is a pretty simple course, there's a LOT of information. Other faculties no matter how lenient or easy-going they are will not compromise when it comes to information. They will expect you to remember articles/sections/cases etc. But not RGC. He'll just tell you to write an example explaining the case/similar/relevant to the case. It doesn't have to be a real example, you can create one out of your own imagination AS LONG AS IT is answers the question properly. He expects quality > quantity though. He discourages writing 69 pages of irrelevant material for a 20 mark question. He rather asks the students to write exactly to the point without too much of excessive detail. And he marks VERY leniently. I don't think that he curves but, considering how generously he marks, you don't even need curving to get a good grade. He doesn't take any assignments or presentation or whatsoever though. He takes 2 quizzes (Best 1) on a scale of 10 and then converts the marks to 20 (example if you get 8, it becomes 16, if 9 it becomes 18) 1 mid - 30 marks (2 out of 4 questions worth 15 marks each) and final exam - 40 marks (2 out of 4 questions worth 20 marks each) I am telling you again, do not get startled looking at how much marks the questions carry. Only write as much as you need. The better you can explain using lesser words, the better your score is gonna be.
SHA1 - ACT201
Boyosh hoise 24. Ei boyoshe eshe teacher der niye kharap kotha bolar ruchi nai. But, regarding her I'll just say, NOT WORTH IT.
I do not doubt her teaching. I do not think I could have learned accounting better from anybody else. Her teaching is 10/10 HOWEVER, the questions in the exams are 15/10. Sometimes you look at the question and wonder je bhai, uni ki atkanor jonno question korsen naki? Achha thikase, eta nahoy dhorlam amar academic lacking. But, when it comes to behavior, Lord be merciful. Trust me, I am no snowflake. I have survived and did very well under "DROPPPPPP" faculties from my very first semester but all of them were very helpful people regardless. How she behaves is definitely unexpected of in such a prestigious institution. I won't say much because I do not like speaking ill of teachers but I'll mention one incident for context :
She locks the door 15 minutes after the class starts ; no problem with that. But this one day, a classmate of ours came late because he encountered a horrible accident. He had a leg bandaged from toe to knee and the class was on the 5th floor. When he arrived, he knocked a few times since the door was locked. She went out the door, saw his condition and legit SCREAMED at him so loud that I could assure you that all eleven floors of both SAC and NAC heard it. And, she didn't even let him in the class lmao.
Arekta jinish hochhe, onar kothar kono mil nai. In the very first class she said she doesn't curve but in the very next sentence she said depending on attendance and effort she might curve a grade. Mid semester eshe amader bolsen je there's this AI platform (she's probably connected with/is one of the developers) that she wants us to use to do accounting problems (basically train her AI) She said that she'll give bonus marks depending on how much we talk to the AI and had also mentioned that a lot of her students got a significant boost in grades due to bonus marks generated from training the AI (didn't sound convincing anyways) jai hok, ekdom last class e she said she will give 2 marks bonus to everyone and depending on how much they talked to the AI, it might go up to 3/4 marks. I don't think she added those points at all. I've talked to a friend who had done 202 under her last semester. He said that he felt like the same had happened. His raw marks equated to an A- itself so he didn't think there was any curving involved. Ekdin office hour e gesilam to confirm what she plans to do with the grading, first e jhari dilen pore bollen amar mon chaile 10 grade komaye dibo, mon chaile 10 grade baraye dibo, mon chaile deserving tai dibo. You'll get what you deserved. I mean, a simple response would have sufficed, no? Bina karone eto rude howar mane ki?
My mother herself is a teacher and a headmaster in a government school so I understand better than anybody else that teacher der jei workload thake, tar karone shobshomoy mon mejaj bhalo thake na. But not having the basic decency to answer a simple query without snapping at people is a different issue. It's not only me who has experienced such misbehavior. My classmates could relate too.
In conclusion, I have nothing against her. I am merely a peasant in comparison to her accomplishments. Neither do I doubt her teaching quality. But, everything else that comes with it is something that doesn't sit right with me. Drop or keep? Up to you, honestly. But, I wouldn't recommend keeping unless you're very good at accounting from before your university life and if you're not somebody that's okay with letting people walk over you.
BUS112 - MMR5
Believe me when I say good faculties from JU exist because he is one of them. He radiates a very 'cool uncle' energy in the class. His classes are fun and interactive. Although the course itself is very simple, MMR5 breaks it down into even simpler pieces for the students to absorb it easier. If you're somebody that fears math/has forgotten what you studied during 9-12 grade, HE is the man for you. Ekdom shohoj kothay, sir ekdom bachhader muukhe tule diye jebhabe khaway thik oibhabei topic gula poraye den. On top of that he is VERY lenient. He marks very graciously. Partial marking eo kiptami koren na. ONEK curve koren and bonus points if your attendance is 100% I was initially skeptical je nibo ki nibona cause I am sh!t at math but, I don't think I could've found a better faculty to teach me things I had forgotten long ago. He takes 3 quizzes- 20 marks each (Best 2) 1 mid - 30 marks 2 assignments and final exam - 35 marks. And he is a very approachable person so if you have problems/don't understand a math he will repeat over and over again for you. BUT, one factor to consider is : Sir er kisu topic/content dekhe mone hote pare je egula na poraileo cholto, hudai extra porachhen. But, honestly, considering how generously he grades and how the questions mostly come from the slides, I don't have much to complain. One thing I would recommend is, if you take the course under him, practice the math on a daily so that it makes your life easier. Quiz/mid/final er thik ager muhurte grind kora ta moderately risky unless you're VERY good at math. In overall, GOATED ekta faculty.
Tnn - MGT351
This is my 2nd course under Tnn and it saddens me that I won't get a third to do under her. She's probably the most standard faculty I've come across so far ; strict but only as much as she needs to be. She won't do you outstanding favors but she won't make your lives miserable either. In order to do well, you have to attend classes regularly and engage as much as you can. The questions in the exam are very standard I would say ; Easy if you're up to date with your studies. Nothing ever comes outside of the slides and she provides suggestions before the exam. She takes 2 quizzes (;est 1) worth 10 marks, a case study, 1 mid (25 marks) report + presentation (20 marks) and final exam (30 marks) she might be very picky when it comes to answers in the exams. Writing too much might get your marks deducted. She too prefers writing to the very point ; only as much as you need. If you're the kind of person that has a "bujhaye likhe dibo" tendency, think twice. You can write your ideas around the main topic keeping them central but not the other way around. This will get you negative marking. And she is really strict when it comes to presentation. Each group will get no longer than 10 minutes and there will be a lot of questions after the presentation from the faculty. If you know what is written on the report, you'll be able to answer or else no. The questions are pretty straightforward. Faculty Initial: TTR

Faculty reviews before the next sem 
BUS112 (REK) - It was my first semester, that too online. Sir made sure everyone participated in the class by asking them to explain things after he had explained them first. His teaching style was very thorough and he gave a lot of assignments so we had a lot of chance to practice and prepare for the exams. His grading was good too, he was fair and also curved. 
ENG103 (NNM) - I had a hard time following her lectures because they were boring and she was also very uncooperative, but could be because of the online classes. Her quizzes and exams were easy but I felt she did not grade students fairly, and was biased.
POL101 (RZK) - For me, the course itself was not very interesting so I felt sir’s teaching was average as well. I did not enjoy it, but I could get through it. Sir made questions directly from the slides and also grades fairly. 
ECO101 (MUF) - Sir is very old, so I was very grateful that he made so much efforts to teach us, that to online. The lectures weren’t fun tho, exams were not easy neither hard, and he graded fairly. 
MGT212 and MKT330 (ZMC) - In both the courses I thoroughly enjoyed her class. She puts a lot of efforts into making the lectures enjoyable and she also gives hints about the exams. She grades very strictly but fairly. But most importantly she’s very compassionate and empathetic towards her students and excuses a lot of things simply for them to pass the course. 
MKT202 and MKT344 (FCH) - Her lectures are very elaborative and she makes sure all the students understand them. She gives a lot of opportunities for bonus marking as well. She is very strict tho but as long as you are a attentive and sincere student you’re good to go. Are exams are tricky and critical and she grades fairly. She’s also very no-nonsense.
ACT201 (FJM) - His teaching style is average, but his grading is biased. He’s also a little rude. I would not suggest to take his course. 
ECO104 (NNM) - Miss is very sweet, she teaches really well. Her exams aren’t very hard either and her grading style is fair. 
LAW200 (TTR) - Again, miss is really sweet. I really enjoyed her exams. She’s also very understanding. Her exams are easy to score in, and she grades fairly. 
ENG105 (RT1) - Just drop the courses. She’s inconsiderate, uncooperative and does not teach well. I dropped it before my mids. 
ACT202 (RMH1) - I think sir is one of the best faculties for this course. He teaches really well, his exams are easy to perform in if you follow his lecture and he grades fairly. 
BUS172 (KHS) - Sir is very strict but he’s also probably one of the best faculties in NSU. He teaches extremely well, is also very helpful. And he curves a lot. 
ENG105 (MCD) - She’s very strict, but she teaches really well. She’ll do her best to guide you in every step so that you get the grade you deserve. 
INB372 (TFZ) - Miss is fun and caring. Her teaching style is easy to catch. Her exams are super easy too and she grades really well. 
PHI401 (BAI) - I had a hard time with this course, but I think PHI is just boring and not really Sir’s fault. He gives a lot of chances to makeup for any lost grade. 
BUS251 (UHM) - One of my favourite faculties. The course itself is very easy and UMH makes it a walk in the park. Her activities are really fun and she gives a lot of chances to score. She also prepares you really well for the exams so there’s no chance that you won’t get your deserving grade. 
PSY101 (FHK) - Miss is really fun. Even though it’s offline classes now she takes the quizzes online. She is very generous with marking too. 
SOC101 (IZS) - I saved it for the last because miss has some very controversial reviews. Yes it is a GED course and yet miss makes you work very hard for it. You have to watch movies, tons of videos, read the slides, books, and other materials to score well. But she also teaches really well, her classes are fun to follow and very interactive. She also grades very well. You just need to study. 
BUS173 (RSJ) - Ma’am taught amazingly. I struggle with maths but she made it reality easy to catch on. She also gave students chances to sit for exams if they missed it due to proper reason. Her exams were also not hard. However, I felt like she was biased and helped her favourite students during exams and hence she might not have graded us all fairly. 
These are just my experiences with the faculties and you may agree or disagree but I hope this helps people who are planning to take these courses. See less

Tanjil Kabir
★ LAW200, TTR
TEACHING: teaches very well, explains everything very simply with examples. explains the case laws in an easy to remember way but you need some effort to understand the whole thing and to remember the sections.
GRADING:
- QUIZ (15 marks) she takes 2 quizzes, counts best 1. if you do well in quiz 1 or satisfied with your marks she allows you to skip quiz 2. 10 MCQs and 2 short questions.
- MID (30 marks): only has problem questions and essay questions. for problem questions you need to follow the IRAC writing method, she gives suggestions for problem questions and questions come from the suggestions. for essay questions she'll give a more general idea but you need to have a good grasp of the overall syllabus.
you can EASILY get full marks in quizzes and mid as she's pretty generous with marking.
- PRESENTATION (10 marks): she will assign the topic to each group. 5 marks for group cohesiveness, slides, group’s overall alignment and 5 marks for individual speeches. she doesn't ask questions after presentation, only gives a review about slides and content. she mostly looks at how much research you've done about your assigned topic.
- ATTENDANCE(10 marks): can miss up to 3 classes and she might consider more if you have an actual valid reason.
- FINALS (40 marks): MCQs, Problem Questions and Essay Questions. the questions in finals were a bit tricky compared to MID but pretty standard nonetheless.
Overall, i would say if you're aiming for straight A on LAW200, there can't be a better faculty than Ratry ma'am. she's exceptionally good.
EXTRA: her classes maybe a little long at times and she uses notes instead slides so it may seem like there's a lot of content but when you actually study you'll realize it's really not much at all. she only keeps the basics, very streamlined outline. she makes the course very easy for everyone and is an excellent teacher. you'll get through the course very smoothly with a very good grade if you get her.
[
N.B. Faculty Reviews are SUBJECTIVE.]
